summary.text: Introduces the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP, Saaty 1977, 1990), explaining how a decision hierarchy of Goal, Criteria, and Alternatives (Figure 8.1) is evaluated through subjective pairwise comparisons on Saaty's 1–9 scale (begun in Table 8.4) to derive criteria weights via the principal eigenvector or sum-normalization approximation without requiring an ACM.

sections.extract: Preliminary Draft Manuscript 8-7 The AHP method, originally developed by Saaty (1977, 1990), is based on decision-makers’ subjective pairwise comparisons. To facilitate this, Saaty’s fundamental 1–9 scale (Table 8.4) is typically employed. The AHP method begins by constructing a decision hierarchy, organizing the overall goal, 𝑛 criteria, and 𝑚 alternatives into a structured model, as illustrated in Figure 8.1.

sections.title: Page 8

summary.text: Completes Table 8.4 (Saaty's 1–9 pairwise comparison scale and reciprocals) and explains how AHP acts as a full MCDM method: constructing n pairwise comparison matrices (m x m) of alternatives per criterion—either from subjective judgments or by mapping objective ACM data onto the 1–9 scale—deriving local priority vectors via the eigenvalue method, and multiplying by the criteria weight vector to obtain global priorities.
